baseline_prompt_en: A photographic mecha scene makes the constructed body of a mechanical subject legible through a visible encounter between human and machine. In the closed repair kiosk of a seaside ferry terminal after the final departure, a human-sized service robot sits on the left of a narrow workbench while a short-haired woman sits on the right, close enough to work. Use the supplied portrait for the woman's face and hair appearance: preserve the visible facial proportions, dark eyes, short dark bob and wispy separated fringe. Her plain navy work shirt has its sleeves rolled back. Her quietly absorbed expression and relaxed mouth give her an unforced, subtly attractive presence. The robot has a compact rounded head, a small optical face, a plainly mechanical neck and worn pale industrial body panels. It places its opened left forearm across a folded cloth on the bench, palm turned upward. A removed forearm cover rests beside it. The woman steadies the exposed forearm frame with her left hand while her right hand seats a small driver against an accessible screw near the wrist. Her elbows stay outside the opened cavity. The robot's free hand holds the detached cover steady on the workbench. Their heads incline toward the same repair point, suggesting concentrated cooperation rather than a display pose. Compose a horizontal medium photograph from a front three-quarter viewpoint at bench height, with the woman's face, both working hands, the robot's head and the entire open forearm visible together. Give the open machinery substantial space in the lower center. A warm task lamp separates bare metal from the cool dark windows and a faint reflection of the empty boarding hall. Restrained color, tactile wear, natural skin texture and clear depth make this a believable documentary photograph of an invented ordinary night.
